decode.scroll_stop_trick: Three hand-drawn torsos in a row — soft, softer, flat — with WEEK 0 / WEEK 2 / WEEK 4 chalk labels and a chalkboard banner saying goodbye to the belly. Looks like a doctor's sketch, not an ad.
decode.angle_carried: dad bod belly, 4-week timeline — Adrien kept their words ('GOODBYE DAD BOD BELLY')
decode.hidden_reading: a drawing promises less than a photo and is believed more — anatomy-book authority
decode.scene_logic: three stages of the same body left to right; ours = the same man's torso, belly over the waistband at week 0, less round at week 2, flat (not muscular) at week 4
decode.visual_trick: the cross-hatched pencil style and the chalkboard labels; copy literally
decode.shape_or_function_equivalent: six-pack at week 4 ↔ a flat, normal 50-year-old torso at week 4 (our avatar never gets abs); amber bottle ↔ pouch
decode.render_style: black pencil and ink sketch on white paper, cross-hatching, no colour
decode.text_treatment: white chalk capitals on black rounded labels; long black banner with white chalk text

strategy.angle: A8-M the man's belly that isn't fat — the keg that no diet moved
strategy.mechanism: M1: when the body can't clear everyday oxidative stress, the tissue in the legs stays inflamed and stops draining normally, so fluid sits there — heavy, tender, puffy — and no diet reaches it, because it was never fat; the tablet turns a glass of water into hydrogen-rich water, hydrogen is the smallest molecule there is, reaches the tissue and helps the body switch that process off so normal drainage can resume
strategy.sub_avatar: trigger: belt notch, the 'dad bod' joke · cause: inflamed tissue holding fluid · tried: sit-ups, skipping beer, intermittent fasting
strategy.belief_installed: A belly that no diet moves isn't food I stored — it's what my body stopped clearing.
